style.ownership: components own nested components, private data, ports and functions; functions own calculations and flow or states
style.scope: Original SWAML notation, organized in a SysML-style reference table; not an OMG notation conformance claim.

concepts.title: Package
concepts.context: Package header; declarations occupy its body.
rules: Draw a tabbed rectangular namespace frame; the tab contains the package name.
Nested compartments show owned declarations, not runtime instances created by package membership.
concepts.description: Package. Draw a tabbed rectangular namespace frame; the tab contains the package name.

concepts.title: Package import
concepts.context: Inside package Notation; the target package is loaded in the same workspace.
rules: Draw a dashed open-arrow dependency from the importing package to the imported package, labeled import Shared::*.
This is namespace visibility only; it MUST NOT resemble or create an interface communication route.
concepts.description: Package import. Draw a dashed open-arrow dependency from the importing package to the imported package, labeled import Shared::*.

concepts.title: Component definition
concepts.context: Reusable component type header inside package Hello.
rules: Draw a sharp-corner classifier rectangle with the component double-tab marker and explicit «component def» heading above its type name.
Separate the name from ports, child instances, private data and functions; definitions do not allocate singleton state.
concepts.description: Component definition. Draw a sharp-corner classifier rectangle with the component double-tab marker and explicit «component def» heading above its type name.

concepts.title: Component usage
concepts.context: Contained component occurrence in root Hello::Demo.
rules: Draw a structural rectangle with the component double-tab marker, labeled conversation: Conversation with «component» visible; preserve occurrence and type names.
Each occurrence has its own path context; two rectangles typed by the same definition MUST NOT merge private storage.
concepts.description: Component usage. Draw a structural rectangle with the component double-tab marker, labeled conversation: Conversation with «component» visible; preserve occurrence and type names.

concepts.title: Component specialization
concepts.context: Reusable definition ComponentReuse::FastWorker specializes Worker.
concepts.description: Single inheritance reuses the base component’s effective members while each instance keeps independent state.
rules: Draw a solid generalization line from the derived definition to the base, ending in an unfilled triangle at the base and labeled specializes.
The link connects definitions, not running instances. It does not create an extra component instance or shared private store.
Inherited members may be replaced only through compatible explicit redefines declarations.

concepts.title: Member redefinition
concepts.context: Replacement function owned by ComponentReuse::FastWorker.
concepts.description: An explicit redefinition replaces an inherited member in the derived component’s effective feature set.
rules: Prefix the owned member label with redefines and preserve its member kind, name and compatible contract.
Port, variable, child, function, connector and delegation replacements use their ordinary glyphs with this explicit label.
Display one effective member for the derived instance; an override does not allocate another behavior or store.

concepts.title: Occurrence typing relationship
concepts.context: Occurrence typing in Hello::Demo; the same type identity is normally shown by the name: Type label.
rules: When typing is shown as a separate relationship, draw a dashed line with a hollow triangular arrowhead pointing from the occurrence to its definition and label it type.
This is a typing dependency, never inheritance, delegation or a communication route; the name: Type label remains authoritative.
concepts.description: Occurrence typing relationship. A dashed type arrow points from the occurrence to its reusable definition.

concepts.title: Root component
concepts.context: Top-level named occurrence; its type is Roots::Pair.
rules: Draw a containing component frame labeled «root component» and the selected occurrence name/type.
Root selection is explicit; the frame is composition context and MUST NOT be drawn as an executable function or another authored system element.
concepts.description: Root component. Draw a containing component frame labeled «root component» and the selected occurrence name/type.

concepts.title: Inline root composition
concepts.context: Top-level inline component occurrence in Roots.
rules: Draw a root component frame with its owned members: child components, private data, functions and typed routes.
The root is a closed instance: owned ports participate only in explicit connections or delegation, with no implicit external peer.
concepts.description: An inline top-level component directly owns its architecture and local behavior.

concepts.title: Record datatype
concepts.syntax: datatype Measurement { value: real; health: Health; }
concepts.context: Nominal datatype declaration inside Values.
rules: Draw a classifier rectangle headed «datatype» and the nominal type name, followed by a field compartment.
Fields retain declared names/types; identical-looking declarations remain distinct nominal types.
concepts.description: Record datatype. Draw a classifier rectangle headed «datatype» and the nominal type name, followed by a field compartment.

concepts.title: Enumeration
concepts.context: Nominal enum declaration inside Values.
rules: Draw a classifier rectangle headed «enum», with one literal per row in a literals compartment.
The literal order is display order, not an implied integer encoding or state-transition order.
concepts.description: Enumeration. Draw a classifier rectangle headed «enum», with one literal per row in a literals compartment.

concepts.title: Primitive types
concepts.context: void is shown as an interface result; other primitive types label fields/parameters/results.
rules: Display bool, byte, uint, int, real, string or void as textual type labels in the owning compartment.
byte is 0–255 and uint is a nonnegative safe integer. Integral narrowing checks the destination domain; real does not implicitly narrow.
void labels function results only; an omitted function result means void.
concepts.description: Basic data types label values and signatures; fixed arrays, nominal records and enums build on them.

concepts.title: Parameter or record field
concepts.context: Function signature fragment inside Hello::Listener.
rules: Show ordered parameters as name: Type within the function signature; show record fields as name: Type rows in their datatype.
Parameter order is semantic; a graphical editor MUST retain it when reordering unrelated compartments.
concepts.description: Parameter or record field. Show ordered parameters as name: Type within the function signature; show record fields as name: Type rows in their datatype.

concepts.title: Private component variable
concepts.context: Private values compartment of Hello::Listener.
rules: Show a var name: Type = initializer row inside its component boundary.
Do not draw shared-storage connectors to this row; another component cannot read or write it directly.
concepts.description: Private component variable. Show a var name: Type = initializer row inside its component boundary.

concepts.title: Pure calculation
concepts.syntax: calc twice { in x: real; return result: real = x * 2.0; }
concepts.context: Calculation declared at the start of Values::Producer.prepare.
rules: Draw a flat calculation compartment inside its owning function, headed calc and its name.
List each input with in and its type; show return, the output name/type and expression in a separate row.
A calculation call is local expression text such as twice(samples[i]); it is not a message or independent executable function.
concepts.description: A calculation maps named inputs to one named, typed output expression without mutable state or communication.

concepts.title: Record construction
concepts.syntax: record Measurement { value = twice(samples[i]); health = Health.Good; }
concepts.context: Initializer fragment inside Values::Producer.prepare; samples and i are local values.
rules: Display record construction as expression text attached to its owning statement/field, with the nominal type visible.
All declared fields are present exactly once; a record value MUST NOT be drawn as a mutable component occurrence.
concepts.description: Record construction. Display record construction as expression text attached to its owning statement/field, with the nominal type visible.

concepts.title: Enumeration value
concepts.context: Expression inside Values::Producer.prepare.
rules: Render the exact nominal value text Type.Literal, or Package::Type.Literal when qualification is needed.
An accessible local first segment denotes a value-field read instead; the graphic MUST preserve the resolved identity rather than guessing from the dot.
concepts.description: Enumeration value. Render the exact nominal value text Type.Literal, or Package::Type.Literal when qualification is needed.

concepts.title: Fixed array type and value
concepts.context: Local declaration in Values::Producer.prepare.
rules: Display fixed extent in the type label T[n] and ordered elements in brackets within the owning expression.
Array elements are copied values; no array icon may imply reference-valued payloads or dynamic multiplicity.
concepts.description: Fixed array type and value. Display fixed extent in the type label T[n] and ordered elements in brackets within the owning expression.

concepts.title: Expressions and value paths
concepts.syntax: assert not false and (1 + 2 * 3 >= 7) or true;
concepts.context: Expression inside Notation::Sink.check.
rules: Keep literals, operators, parentheses and value paths as expression text in the owning label or compartment.
Expression layout MUST preserve precedence and short-circuit order; it does not add flow nodes for operators unless the fv is explicitly an explanatory expansion.
concepts.description: Expressions and value paths. Keep literals, operators, parentheses and value paths as expression text in the owning label or compartment.

concepts.title: Sender–receiver interface
concepts.context: Interface declaration header; member rows occupy the contract body.
rules: Draw an interface classifier rectangle with the exact interface kind, nominal name and version in its heading.
Keep member categories visible; a contract box is a reusable type and MUST NOT be mistaken for a runtime broker or component.
concepts.description: Sender–receiver interface. Draw an interface classifier rectangle with the exact interface kind, nominal name and version in its heading.

concepts.title: Client–server interface
concepts.context: Interface declaration header; member rows occupy the contract body.
rules: Draw an interface classifier rectangle with the exact interface kind, nominal name and version in its heading.
Keep member categories visible; a contract box is a reusable type and MUST NOT be mistaken for a runtime broker or component.
concepts.description: Client–server interface. Draw an interface classifier rectangle with the exact interface kind, nominal name and version in its heading.

concepts.title: Publish–subscribe interface
concepts.context: Interface declaration header; member rows occupy the contract body.
rules: Draw an interface classifier rectangle with the exact interface kind, nominal name and version in its heading.
Keep member categories visible; a contract box is a reusable type and MUST NOT be mistaken for a runtime broker or component.
concepts.description: Publish–subscribe interface. Draw an interface classifier rectangle with the exact interface kind, nominal name and version in its heading.

concepts.title: Service interface
concepts.context: Interface declaration header; member rows occupy the contract body.
rules: Draw an interface classifier rectangle with the exact interface kind, nominal name and version in its heading.
Keep member categories visible; a contract box is a reusable type and MUST NOT be mistaken for a runtime broker or component.
concepts.description: Service interface. Draw an interface classifier rectangle with the exact interface kind, nominal name and version in its heading.

concepts.title: Data member
concepts.context: Member of Control::Samples; queued is the alternative retention mode.
rules: Show data name: Type and sampled or queued on one interface-compartment row.
Retention mode is explicit text, not color; sampled uses latest-value buffering while queued retains individual values under QoS.
concepts.description: Data member. Show data name: Type and sampled or queued on one interface-compartment row.

concepts.title: Event member
concepts.context: Member of Lifecycle::Status.
rules: Show event name(parameters) in its interface compartment; draw no free-floating event definition.
Every graphical emission or receive label identifies this member through an owned port and function.
concepts.description: Event member. Show event name(parameters) in its interface compartment; draw no free-floating event definition.

concepts.title: Interface function signature
concepts.context: RPC contract member of Rpc::Health.
rules: Show function name(parameters): Result and idempotent when declared, inside the interface contract.
The signature is distinct from its component implementation; a contract row has no executable body.
concepts.description: Interface function signature. Show function name(parameters): Result and idempotent when declared, inside the interface contract.

concepts.title: Data sender port
concepts.context: Port declaration on the displayed component boundary.
rules: Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.
Data flows outward from the owned port. Do not infer direction only from left/right placement; role text remains mandatory.
concepts.description: Data sender port. Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.

concepts.title: Data receiver port
concepts.context: Port declaration on the displayed component boundary.
rules: Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.
Data flows inward to the owned receiving function. Do not infer direction only from left/right placement; role text remains mandatory.
concepts.description: Data receiver port. Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.

concepts.title: RPC client port
concepts.context: Port declaration on the displayed component boundary.
rules: Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.
Requests leave and correlated results return through this same port. Do not infer direction only from left/right placement; role text remains mandatory.
concepts.description: RPC client port. Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.

concepts.title: RPC server port
concepts.context: Port declaration on the displayed component boundary.
rules: Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.
Requests enter and correlated results leave through this same port. Do not infer direction only from left/right placement; role text remains mandatory.
concepts.description: RPC server port. Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.

concepts.title: Event publisher port
concepts.context: Port declaration on the displayed component boundary.
rules: Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.
Events leave this port through explicit subscription connectors. Do not infer direction only from left/right placement; role text remains mandatory.
concepts.description: Event publisher port. Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.

concepts.title: Event subscriber port
concepts.context: Port declaration on the displayed component boundary.
rules: Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.
Events enter the declared handling function through this port. Do not infer direction only from left/right placement; role text remains mandatory.
concepts.description: Event subscriber port. Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.

concepts.title: Service provider port
concepts.context: Port declaration on the displayed component boundary.
rules: Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.
RPC requests enter; results and provider events leave. Do not infer direction only from left/right placement; role text remains mandatory.
concepts.description: Service provider port. Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.

concepts.title: Service consumer port
concepts.context: Port declaration on the displayed component boundary.
rules: Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.
RPC requests leave; results and provider events enter. Do not infer direction only from left/right placement; role text remains mandatory.
concepts.description: Service consumer port. Draw a small square centered on the owning boundary and label its name: Interface and exact role.

concepts.title: Optional port
concepts.context: Reusable component NotationOptions::Emitter; its outgoing member is tied to an function.
rules: Use the same square port symbol and append optional to its role label.
Optionality only permits an unconnected route; it does not remove contract, provenance or receiving-handler obligations.
concepts.description: Optional port. Use the same square port symbol and append optional to its role label.

concepts.title: Interface connector
concepts.syntax: connect greeting: speaker.output -> listener.input qos { delivery atMostOnce; ordering fifo; capacity 4; overflow reject; };
concepts.context: Connection between immediate child ports of Hello::Conversation.
rules: Draw a solid directed connector between port squares, with connector identity and interface name visible.
The arrow follows declared source-to-target roles; replies/service events reverse that route rather than creating a second hidden channel.
concepts.description: Interface connector. Draw a solid directed connector between port squares, with connector identity and interface name visible.

concepts.title: Boundary delegation
concepts.context: Boundary-to-immediate-child alias inside Settings::Service.
rules: Draw a solid unarrowed line labeled delegate from a boundary port to one immediate child port inside its owner.
Both endpoints keep identical interface identity and role; this alias creates no queue, service call, adapter or extra message.
concepts.description: Boundary delegation. Draw a solid unarrowed line labeled delegate from a boundary port to one immediate child port inside its owner.

concepts.title: Delivery policy
concepts.context: QoS property on Rpc::HealthCheck.healthCheck; the signature is idempotent.
rules: Attach a QoS property compartment to its connector; write the exact delivery value.
atLeastOnce, atMostOnce and bestEffort are textual alternatives, not three different edge shapes; atLeastOnce RPC requires idempotent signatures.
concepts.description: Delivery policy. Attach a QoS property compartment to its connector; write the exact delivery value.

concepts.title: Queue ordering
concepts.context: QoS property on Notation::Demo.events.
rules: Write ordering fifo or ordering unordered in the connector QoS compartment.
Ordering applies per route, direction and member; line position or crossing MUST NOT imply a global order.
concepts.description: Queue ordering. Write ordering fifo or ordering unordered in the connector QoS compartment.

concepts.title: Queue capacity
concepts.context: QoS property on Hello::Conversation.greeting.
rules: Write the positive capacity value in the connector QoS compartment.
Capacity counts pending logical messages for the route/direction/member; do not encode capacity as line thickness.
concepts.description: Queue capacity. Write the positive capacity value in the connector QoS compartment.

concepts.title: Overflow behavior
concepts.context: QoS property on Notation::Demo.events.
rules: Write overflow plus dropNewest, dropOldest or reject in the connector QoS compartment.
The label determines retention/rejection semantics; no style variation may silently substitute another policy.
concepts.description: Overflow behavior. Write overflow plus dropNewest, dropOldest or reject in the connector QoS compartment.

concepts.title: Transport latency bound
concepts.context: QoS bound on Control::Controller.measured.
rules: Write maxLatency and an explicitly component-bearing duration beside the corresponding connector.
This bound ends at transport readiness; it MUST NOT be labeled as total execution or dispatch deadline.
concepts.description: Transport latency bound. Write maxLatency and an explicitly component-bearing duration beside the corresponding connector.

concepts.title: Message freshness bound
concepts.context: QoS freshness bound on Control::Controller.measured.
rules: Write maxAge and its explicit component in the connector QoS compartment.
Age is measured from original emission, including retries; show expiry as a trace observation only when supported by a run.
concepts.description: Message freshness bound. Write maxAge and its explicit component in the connector QoS compartment.

concepts.title: Executable function
concepts.context: Header of Hello::Speaker.greet; its statement body is projected inside the function frame.
rules: Draw an function frame or compartment with its name, ordered parameters, result and activation label.
Every fv step is an owned statement projection within this frame; it MUST NOT create an independently allocated action or performer.
concepts.description: Executable function. Draw an function frame or compartment with its name, ordered parameters, result and activation label.

concepts.title: Startup activation
concepts.context: Activation annotation on the displayed function.
rules: Attach the activation text to its function header; use no free event symbol or standalone trigger object.
Once after component initialization and route readiness.
concepts.description: Startup activation. Attach the activation text to its function header; use no free event symbol or standalone trigger object.

concepts.title: Manual activation
concepts.context: Activation annotation on the displayed function.
rules: Attach the activation text to its function header; use no free event symbol or standalone trigger object.
Harness activation carries no modeled data; external commands still use ports.
concepts.description: Manual activation. Attach the activation text to its function header; use no free event symbol or standalone trigger object.

concepts.title: Periodic activation
concepts.context: Activation annotation on the displayed function.
rules: Attach the activation text to its function header; use no free event symbol or standalone trigger object.
Release occurs at positive multiples of the declared period.
concepts.description: Periodic activation. Attach the activation text to its function header; use no free event symbol or standalone trigger object.

concepts.title: Port receive activation
concepts.context: Activation annotation on the displayed function.
rules: Attach the activation text to its function header; use no free event symbol or standalone trigger object.
The port/member label identifies the one incoming handler owner.
concepts.description: Port receive activation. Attach the activation text to its function header; use no free event symbol or standalone trigger object.

concepts.title: RPC handler activation
concepts.context: Activation annotation on the displayed function.
rules: Attach the activation text to its function header; use no free event symbol or standalone trigger object.
Requests and correlated results remain on the originating interface route.
concepts.description: RPC handler activation. Attach the activation text to its function header; use no free event symbol or standalone trigger object.

concepts.title: Local declaration
concepts.context: Statement inside the displayed owning function; the fv node is a projection.
rules: Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.
Creates a copied typed local value in the enclosing lexical block.
concepts.description: Local declaration. Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.

concepts.title: Assignment
concepts.context: Statement inside the displayed owning function; the fv node is a projection.
rules: Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.
Replaces an existing permitted whole value; a field path or another component is not an assignment target.
concepts.description: Assignment. Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.

concepts.title: Local function call
concepts.context: Statement inside the displayed owning function; the fv node is a projection.
rules: Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.
Calls an untriggered flow function in the same component, borrowing its activation lock/snapshot. Bind a non-void result with as name; omit the binding for void.
concepts.description: Local function invocation. Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.

concepts.title: Data send
concepts.context: Statement inside the displayed owning function; the fv node is a projection.
rules: Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.
The text identifies the emitting function’s owned sender port and data member.
concepts.description: Data send. Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.

concepts.title: Event publication
concepts.context: Statement inside the displayed owning function; the fv node is a projection.
rules: Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.
The text identifies the emitting function’s owned publisher/provider port and event member.
concepts.description: Event publication. Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.

concepts.title: Assertion
concepts.context: Statement inside the displayed owning function; the fv node is a projection.
rules: Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.
False fails the activation; this step is an execution check, not proof of a requirement.
concepts.description: Assertion. Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.

concepts.title: Failure
concepts.context: Statement inside the displayed owning function; the fv node is a projection.
rules: Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.
Failure unwinds the activation without rollback; it does not imply an unmodeled broadcast.
concepts.description: Failure. Draw an owned statement box with the exact statement label and directed control-flow succession.

concepts.title: Routed function call
concepts.syntax: call setting.get() as observed within 100 ms otherwise { return; };
concepts.context: Statement in Settings::Panel.refresh; successful completion binds observed.
rules: Draw one request step labeled port.member, result binding and timeout, with distinct success and otherwise continuations.
The failure continuation remains explicit and terminating; request arrows outside this function must use the corresponding interface route.
concepts.description: RPC request and failure continuation. Draw one request step labeled port.member, result binding and timeout, with distinct success and otherwise continuations.

concepts.title: Function return
concepts.context: Return statement in Rpc::Server.checkHealth.
rules: Show a labeled return terminal in the owning function flow; retain the returned expression when present.
Return from a helper resumes its local caller; return from a state body terminates the owning stateful function.
concepts.description: Function return. Show a labeled return terminal in the owning function flow; retain the returned expression when present.

concepts.title: Conditional branch
concepts.syntax: if (duty > 0.8) { send output.duty(0.8); } else { send output.duty(duty); }
concepts.context: If/else statement in Control::Regulator.regulate.
rules: Draw a decision diamond with the bool condition and distinct true/false control exits, followed by a merge when control continues.
Exactly one branch executes; the diamond is an if-statement projection, not an independent behavior definition.
concepts.description: Conditional branch. Draw a decision diamond with the bool condition and distinct true/false control exits, followed by a merge when control continues.

concepts.title: Bounded loop
concepts.context: Loop header in Values::Producer.prepare; the body is rendered as the loop compartment.
rules: Draw a loop frame with explicit while condition and positive bound label, and a return control edge for iteration.
The bound is semantic, not decoration; a still-true condition after the limit leads to failure rather than silent completion.
concepts.description: Bounded loop. Draw a loop frame with explicit while condition and positive bound label, and a return control edge for iteration.

concepts.title: Function with states
concepts.context: Function header in Lifecycle::Device; its direct body begins with initial.
rules: Draw the state graph inside the owning function frame, keeping the function name and on start label visible.
There is no machine box, performer, or separate authored state allocation; StateBody contributes only the function’s contents.
concepts.description: Function with states. Draw the state graph inside the owning function frame, keeping the function name and on start label visible.

concepts.title: Initial state reference
concepts.context: First clause of Lifecycle::Device.lifecycle.
rules: Draw a solid initial pseudonode with one outgoing unlabeled initialization edge to the named initial state.
This projects the function’s unique initial reference; it is not a transmitted event or a second start function.
concepts.description: Initial state reference. Draw a solid initial pseudonode with one outgoing unlabeled initialization edge to the named initial state.

concepts.title: State
concepts.context: State declaration in Notation::Controller.lifecycle.
rules: Draw a rounded state rectangle bearing the function-local state name, with optional entry/exit compartments.
State rectangles live inside one owning function; position does not allocate them to components or performers.
concepts.description: State. Draw a rounded state rectangle bearing the function-local state name, with optional entry/exit compartments.

concepts.title: Final state
concepts.context: Named final state inside Notation::Controller.lifecycle.
rules: Draw a named final-state symbol with a bullseye marker; preserve the declared name and any entry behavior.
No outgoing transition is permitted; finality occurs after entry finishes, so the marker MUST NOT hide an entry block.
concepts.description: Final state. Draw a named final-state symbol with a bullseye marker; preserve the declared name and any entry behavior.

concepts.title: State entry behavior
concepts.context: Entry block on Notation::Controller.lifecycle.Idle.
rules: Show entry and its statements in a compartment inside the owning state.
Entry has no incoming payload bindings; its completion starts residence timers.
concepts.description: State entry behavior. Show entry and its statements in a compartment inside the owning state.

concepts.title: State exit behavior
concepts.context: Exit block on Notation::Controller.lifecycle.Idle.
rules: Show exit and its statements in a compartment inside the owning state.
Exit precedes transition effect and state update, and does not inherit the incoming payload environment.
concepts.description: State exit behavior. Show exit and its statements in a compartment inside the owning state.

concepts.title: State transition
concepts.syntax: transition begin: Idle -> Active on receive signal.pulse when (value > 0) priority 1 { count = value; }
concepts.context: Transition in Notation::Controller.lifecycle.
rules: Draw a directed edge between states in the same function; label its identity, stimulus, optional guard/priority and effect.
Receive labels MUST include port.member; the transition edge is local control, not the interface connector carrying the message.
concepts.description: State transition. Draw a directed edge between states in the same function; label its identity, stimulus, optional guard/priority and effect.

concepts.title: Transition guard
concepts.context: Guard on Notation::Controller.lifecycle.begin.
rules: Show the bool guard in brackets or with its explicit when keyword on the transition label.
A false guard disables that transition for the current stimulus; guard text is not a separate executable action.
concepts.description: Transition guard. Show the bool guard in brackets or with its explicit when keyword on the transition label.

concepts.title: Transition priority
concepts.context: Priority on Notation::Controller.lifecycle.begin.
rules: Display priority as an explicit nonnegative integer on a transition label; omitted means zero.
Larger wins only among enabled transitions for the same state and stimulus; it is not an function scheduler priority.
concepts.description: Transition priority. Display priority as an explicit nonnegative integer on a transition label; omitted means zero.

concepts.title: Completion transition
concepts.syntax: transition finish: Active -> Done on completion when (count > 0) {}
concepts.context: Completion transition in Notation::Controller.lifecycle.
rules: Label the state edge on completion explicitly, with its guard if present.
Completion is local to the owning function and MUST NOT be drawn as an emitted global event.
concepts.description: Completion transition. Label the state edge on completion explicitly, with its guard if present.

concepts.title: Residence timer transition
concepts.syntax: transition elapsed: Active -> Done on after 1 s {}
concepts.context: Timer transition in Notation::Controller.lifecycle.
rules: Label the transition on after with an explicit duration and component.
The duration starts after state entry completes; leaving the state cancels that entry generation’s timers.
concepts.description: Residence timer transition. Label the transition on after with an explicit duration and component.

concepts.title: Function timing contract
concepts.syntax: timing { wcet 1 ms; deadline 3 ms; concurrency serial; }
concepts.context: Contract on Control::Sensor.sample.
rules: Attach a timing compartment to the function, listing wcet, deadline and concurrency explicitly.
WCET counts active execution, deadline counts elapsed release-to-completion; the graphic alone supplies no schedulability proof.
concepts.description: Function timing contract. Attach a timing compartment to the function, listing wcet, deadline and concurrency explicitly.

concepts.title: Concurrency mode
concepts.context: Timing property on Settings::SettingStore.read.
rules: Write serial or reentrant in the function timing compartment; no color or parallel-lane icon substitutes for it.
Reentrant activations read dispatch snapshots and cannot mutate component data; helper calls inherit the activation’s lock/snapshot context.
concepts.description: Concurrency mode. Write serial or reentrant in the function timing compartment; no color or parallel-lane icon substitutes for it.

concepts.title: Duration value
concepts.context: Duration value in Roots::Counter.initialize; ns/us/ms/s are explicit alternatives.
rules: Render an integer and its explicit time unit together in timing, period, timeout or state-timer labels.
ns, us, ms and s are label components, not separate symbols; never imply a component from diagram scale.
concepts.description: Duration value. Render an integer and its explicit time unit together in timing, period, timeout or state-timer labels.

concepts.title: Root execution profile
concepts.context: Root header in Gateway; realtime and service are alternative profiles.
rules: Write the selected service, realtime or mixed profile in the root-component header or property compartment.
An omitted profile means service; suppressing a realtime/mixed label MUST NOT weaken the actual model’s timing obligations.
concepts.description: Root execution profile. Write the selected service, realtime or mixed profile in the root-component header or property compartment.

concepts.title: External deployment target
concepts.context: An external system reference in ComponentReuse::Demo.
rules: Draw a flat rectangle headed external system and show the exact reference as text.
A sysml: reference may identify a separately modeled SysML part; SWAML does not resolve or validate that external model.
This endpoint is placement metadata and never grants access to another component’s state.
concepts.description: An external reference identifies the deployment system without introducing a hardware or execution-node definition into SWAML.

concepts.title: Deployment binding
concepts.context: Deployment of one component instance in ComponentReuse::Demo.
rules: Draw a dashed open-arrow allocation link labeled deploy from the component instance to a flat external-system reference.
Show the complete URI-like reference; deployment does not imply that a SysML or infrastructure model was loaded.
Deployment inherits down the component tree unless a descendant supplies a more specific binding.
concepts.description: A deployment binds a component instance or root to an external system reference.

concepts.title: Requirement
concepts.syntax: requirement LimitedDuty { doc /* Applied duty shall be at most 0.8. */ }
concepts.context: Requirement declaration in Control.
rules: Draw a flat requirement rectangle with its name, optional attributes and one doc compartment.
A requirement has no subject; satisfaction and verification are separate relations.
concepts.description: A named obligation with typed attributes and one optional formal specification.

lines: Applied duty shall be at most 0.8.

concepts.title: Use case
concepts.context: Scenario header in Settings; steps reference Cabin’s root-level connectors.
rules: Draw a case frame labeled useCase with its name and selected root.
The of relation references a root; enclosure never changes package ownership.
concepts.description: A use case describes intended use and routed exchanges.

concepts.title: Satisfaction relation
concepts.context: Package-owned design-to-requirement relation.
rules: Draw a dashed open arrow from the design element to the requirement, labeled satisfy.
A satisfaction claim does not establish verification evidence.
concepts.description: Design claims satisfaction of a requirement.

concepts.title: Case data exchange
concepts.syntax: send source.output.value -> sink.input.value via counts label sent;
concepts.context: Step in Notation::Observe; source and destination are immediate child port/member paths.
rules: Draw a sequence arrow between occurrence lifelines labeled send, port.member paths, connector and step label.
The arrow projects an existing sender–receiver route; it creates neither a free event nor a connector by itself.
concepts.description: Case data exchange. Draw a sequence arrow between occurrence lifelines labeled send, port.member paths, connector and step label.

concepts.title: Case event exchange
concepts.syntax: publish settings.api.changed -> front.setting.changed via frontLink after adjust label frontNotice;
concepts.context: Step in Settings::Change, using the reverse event direction of a service route.
rules: Draw a publication arrow labeled publish and the exact connector/member, retaining its step identity.
For service contracts events travel provider-to-consumer; line orientation follows that role even when opposite the connector’s request orientation.
concepts.description: Case event exchange. Draw a publication arrow labeled publish and the exact connector/member, retaining its step identity.

concepts.title: Case request
concepts.syntax: call caller.health.check -> serviceUnit.health.check via healthCheck label sent;
concepts.context: Routed call step in Rpc::Poll.
rules: Draw a request arrow between occurrence lifelines, labeled the member, connector and step identity.
Its later reply must be uniquely correlated by case ancestry and route/member; vertical spacing does not create that relationship.
concepts.description: Case request. Draw a request arrow between occurrence lifelines, labeled the member, connector and step identity.

concepts.title: Correlated case reply
concepts.syntax: reply serviceUnit.health.check -> caller.health.check via healthCheck after sent label answered;
concepts.context: Reply step in Rpc::Poll; after sent identifies its causal request ancestor.
rules: Draw a dashed reply arrow reversing the matching request route and label its step identity and correlation.
A reply cannot be matched by visual proximity alone; preserve the unique causal request ancestor.
concepts.description: Correlated case reply. Draw a dashed reply arrow reversing the matching request route and label its step identity and correlation.

concepts.title: Case causal order
concepts.context: Dependency fragment of Rpc::Poll’s reply step.
rules: Draw an explicitly labeled after dependency between step labels, or show the predecessor in the arrow label.
Unrelated steps remain unordered; source order and vertical placement are layout choices, not happens-before edges.
concepts.description: Case causal order. Draw an explicitly labeled after dependency between step labels, or show the predecessor in the arrow label.

concepts.title: Occurrence lifeline
concepts.context: Occurrence in Rpc::HealthCheck used as a sequence lifeline.
rules: Draw a lifeline headed by the occurrence name: Type and a dashed vertical line.
A lifeline identifies an existing component occurrence; an actor/performer glyph MUST NOT replace a modeled communication boundary.
concepts.description: Occurrence lifeline. Draw a lifeline headed by the occurrence name: Type and a dashed vertical line.

concepts.title: Browser
concepts.context: Package header used as Browser navigation context, not a separate Browser declaration.
rules: Draw a containment/navigation tree of existing packages, definitions, occurrences and owned members.
Browser has no authored view keyword; navigation expansion does not create semantic containment or allocate behavior.
concepts.description: Browser. Draw a containment/navigation tree of existing packages, definitions, occurrences and owned members.

concepts.title: General View
concepts.context: View projection context; syntax refers to an existing semantic subject.
rules: Draw a framed projection titled gv with the semantic subject identity visible; use the canonical element symbols within it.
The view adds presentation only. It MUST NOT introduce new routes, functions, performers or execution semantics.
concepts.description: General View. Draw a framed projection titled gv with the semantic subject identity visible; use the canonical element symbols within it.

concepts.title: Interconnect View
concepts.context: View projection context; syntax refers to an existing semantic subject.
rules: Draw a framed projection titled iv with the semantic subject identity visible; use the canonical element symbols within it.
The view adds presentation only. It MUST NOT introduce new routes, functions, performers or execution semantics.
concepts.description: Interconnect View. Draw a framed projection titled iv with the semantic subject identity visible; use the canonical element symbols within it.

concepts.title: Case View
concepts.context: View projection context; syntax refers to an existing semantic subject.
rules: Draw a framed projection titled cv with the semantic subject identity visible; use the canonical element symbols within it.
The view adds presentation only. It MUST NOT introduce new routes, functions, performers or execution semantics.
concepts.description: Case View. Draw a framed projection titled cv with the semantic subject identity visible; use the canonical element symbols within it.

concepts.title: Sequence View
concepts.context: View projection context; syntax refers to an existing semantic subject.
rules: Draw a framed projection titled sv with the semantic subject identity visible; use the canonical element symbols within it.
The view adds presentation only. It MUST NOT introduce new routes, functions, performers or execution semantics.
concepts.description: Sequence View. Draw a framed projection titled sv with the semantic subject identity visible; use the canonical element symbols within it.

concepts.title: Grid View
concepts.context: View projection context; syntax refers to an existing semantic subject.
rules: Draw a framed projection titled grv with the semantic subject identity visible; use the canonical element symbols within it.
The view adds presentation only. It MUST NOT introduce new routes, functions, performers or execution semantics.
concepts.description: Grid View. Draw a framed projection titled grv with the semantic subject identity visible; use the canonical element symbols within it.

concepts.title: Flow View
concepts.context: View projection context; syntax refers to an existing semantic subject.
rules: Draw a framed projection titled fv with the semantic subject identity visible; use the canonical element symbols within it.
fv supports both statement flow and function-owned states. Keep the owning function frame and never reintroduce separate action/state views or a machine element.
concepts.description: Flow View. Draw a framed projection titled fv with the semantic subject identity visible; use the canonical element symbols within it.

concepts.title: Reusable QoS policy
concepts.syntax: qos def LocalLink { delivery atMostOnce; ordering fifo; capacity 8; overflow reject; }
concepts.context: Package-owned policy in Settings; selected independently by both Cabin connector occurrences.
rules: Draw a flat contract rectangle labeled «qos def» and its name, with all four base fields in a property compartment.
Expose optional latency/age bounds and declaration identity. Reuse shares values only; queues remain per connector occurrence, direction and member.
concepts.description: Named complete connector policy, shown as a flat declaration card. It has no port, behavior, deployment or runtime queue of its own.

concepts.title: Named connector policy
concepts.context: Explicit policy selection on Settings::Cabin.frontLink.
rules: Attach qos PolicyName to the existing typed connector; the name is a reference, not another communication edge.
Inspection exposes the qualified policy identity, effective base fields and bounds. Do not merge connector queues or hide invalid policy uses.
concepts.description: A connector explicitly selects a package-visible QoS declaration while keeping its own route and queue identity.

concepts.title: Requirement attribute
concepts.context: Owned source element in the Assurance example.
rules: Display immutable typed metadata in an attribute compartment or table cell.
Names are unique within their requirement; metadata is not runtime state.
concepts.description: Display immutable typed metadata in an attribute compartment or table cell. Names are unique within their requirement; metadata is not runtime state.

concepts.title: Formal documentation
concepts.syntax: doc /* Every started worker shall store a result of 2. */
concepts.context: Owned source element in the Assurance example.
rules: Draw one labeled doc compartment or one doc table cell for the owner.
Keep multiline formal text distinct from ordinary comment notes.
concepts.description: Draw one labeled doc compartment or one doc table cell for the owner. Keep multiline formal text distinct from ordinary comment notes.

concepts.title: Ordinary comment
concepts.syntax: // Each instance has its own result.
concepts.context: Owned source element in the Assurance example.
rules: Draw a plain rectangular note inside its owner or connected by a plain dashed line.
Each line comment and each block comment remains separate; there is no comment keyword.
concepts.description: Draw a plain rectangular note inside its owner or connected by a plain dashed line. Each line comment and each block comment remains separate; there is no comment keyword.

lines: Each instance has its own result.

concepts.title: Verification case
concepts.context: Owned source element in the Assurance example.
rules: Draw a case frame labeled verificationCase with its name and root context.
Documentation describes the procedure; verify links identify requirements without asserting a passed result.
concepts.description: Draw a case frame labeled verificationCase with its name and root context. Documentation describes the procedure; verify links identify requirements without asserting a passed result.

concepts.title: Verification relation
concepts.context: Owned source element in the Assurance example.
rules: Draw a dashed open arrow from the verification case to the requirement, labeled verify.
A relation expresses verification intent; evidence and outcome are recorded separately.
concepts.description: Draw a dashed open arrow from the verification case to the requirement, labeled verify. A relation expresses verification intent; evidence and outcome are recorded separately.

concepts.title: Filtered view selection
concepts.context: Owned source element in the Assurance example.
rules: Show the selected occurrence paths within the named view frame.
Combine include clauses as a stable union; filters do not alter model ownership or execution.
concepts.description: Show the selected occurrence paths within the named view frame. Combine include clauses as a stable union; filters do not alter model ownership or execution.
